content: Rifaximin is a medication used to treat diarrhea caused by the common bacterium Escherichia coli, often referred to as traveler's diarrhea. It is not suitable for use if you have a fever or bloody diarrhea. This antibiotic is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Additionally, rifaximin is used to manage irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with diarrhea. Before starting rifaximin, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This should also be done each time you receive a refill. To achieve the best results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. For traveler’s diarrhea, continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms resolve after a few days. If diarrhea persists after 1 to 2 days, if you experience bloody diarrhea, or if you develop a fever alongside diarrhea, inform your doctor immediately. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. However, rifaximin may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to the bacterium Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has ended. Seek medical attention if you experience persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, or blood/mucus in your stool. Serious allergic reactions to rifaximin are rare but possible. Symptoms of an allergic reaction may include rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. If these occur, seek immediate medical attention. Before taking rifaximin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other rifamycin antibiotics (such as rifampin or rifabutin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Rifaximin may also interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it is unknown if it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone overdoses on rifaximin and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store rifaximin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
